pages.text: $(thing)Grain Piles$() store loose grain directly on the ground without a container. Grain stored this way decays over time like food. Piles with a solid ceiling above them are considered $(thing)sheltered$() and decay more slowly.

pages.title: Forming a Pile
pages.text: Grain piles have no crafted item. To form one, $(thing)Sneak + Right-Click$() on a sturdy solid surface while holding a valid grain item. A single item is placed into the new pile automatically.$(br2)You can also shift-click to bulk-fill an existing pile from your stack.

pages.title: Inserting and Extracting
pages.text: $(thing)Right-click$() an existing pile with matching grain to add one item at a time.$(br2)$(thing)Right-click$() with an empty hand to extract grain.$(br2)Only one type of grain can be stored per pile. Mixing grain types is not allowed — you will receive a warning if you try.

pages.title: Fill Levels
pages.text: Each pile has 8 visible fill levels. As more grain is added the pile grows taller. When a pile reaches capacity, dropped grain items nearby will overflow upward into a new pile in the air above, or into an adjacent pile already there.

pages.title: Grain Types
pages.text: Built-in supported grains render with their own textures: $(thing)Barley, Corn, Oat, Rice, Rye,$() and $(thing)Wheat$(). Other modded grains tagged as valid pile items will store and function correctly but render using a generic hay fallback appearance until explicit support is added.
